colophon: Thus ends the Bala Raksha made by the gopis, in the tenth book of the Srimad Bhagavatam.

lines.1: May Aja protect your feet; Manimat, your knees; and your thighs,
lines.2: Yajna; Achyuta, your hips; Hayagriva, your belly;
lines.3: Keshava, your heart; Isha, your chest; the Sun, your throat;
lines.4: Vishnu, your arm; Urukrama, your mouth; Ishvara, your head.
lines.5: May the bearer of the discus be before you, and Hari with his mace behind you;
lines.6: the slayer of Madhu and the Unborn, with bow and sword, at your two sides;
lines.7: Urugaya with his conch at the corners; Upendra above;
lines.8: Garuda on the ground below; and Haladhara, the Person, all around.
lines.9: May Hrishikesha guard your senses; Narayana, your breath;
lines.10: the lord of Shvetadvipa, your consciousness; the master of yoga, your mind;
lines.11: Prishnigarbha, your intellect; the supreme Lord, your very self.
lines.12: May Govinda protect you as you play, and Madhava protect you as you sleep;
lines.13: may Vaikuntha guard you as you walk, and the lord of Shri, you as you sit;
lines.14: and may the enjoyer of sacrifice, terror of every seizing spirit, protect you as you eat.
lines.15: Dakinis and Yatudhanis, the Kushmandas, the seizers of infants,
lines.16: ghosts, departed spirits and flesh-eaters, yakshas, rakshasas, and vinayakas,
lines.17: Kotara, Revati, Jyeshtha, Putana, the Matrikas and the rest,
lines.18: the madnesses and the seizures that attack body, breath, and senses,
lines.19: the great portents seen in dreams, the seizers of the old and the young:
lines.20: may they all perish, terrified at the taking of Vishnu's name.
